statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 20% as NQ futures hold inside the overnight range with crude near the day's low and VIX close to unchanged, while Stress stays high on the oil, yield and Fed-repricing backdrop.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 12:00-15:00 UTC window covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with a second single-hour checkpoint at the 21:00 UTC Broadcom call. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold the overnight range as crude eases toward the day's low and volatility stays contained
body: NQ futures traded near 29,072.50 at 08:16 UTC, about 0.18% below the 29,125.50 previous close, with a second independent quote at 29,074.75. The overnight range of 29,016.50-29,170.00 is unchanged from the previous cycle: price has drifted about 34 points lower over the past hour but has made no new low and shows no extension, so the path remains two-way inside an established range. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 1 at 29,077.22, down 1.29%, in a 28,953.26-29,267.42 range, alongside the S&P 500 at 7,631.47 (-0.71%) and the Dow at 52,766.88 (-0.79%). The cross-asset picture continues to de-escalate at the margin. Brent trades near $94.69 against a day range of $94.55-$97.01, so crude is sitting at the low end of its range after Tuesday's roughly 4.6% surge on US strikes against IRGC targets and attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz; WTI is near $90.27. VIX is 16.41, only 0.43% above the 16.34 previous close, which is a notably contained reading given the headline backdrop. The US 10-year yield closed Sep 1 near 4.798%, its highest since January 2025, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 4.75% on the 10-year and 4.34% on the 2-year for Aug 31; Japanese 10-year yields are at their highest since 1996 and UK 30-year yields at their highest since 1998, and fed funds futures price better than a two-in-three chance of an increase at the September 16 FOMC meeting. Asian cash equities fell 2-4% overnight, with the KOSPI near -4% and the Nikkei near -2.9%, yet NQ futures have absorbed that handover within their own range. That combination - a genuinely stressed macro backdrop with an orderly, two-way index price path, easing crude and a flat volatility index - is the decisive Tail observation. Tail is therefore lowered to 20% from 21% and Stress to 71% from 72%. Confidence is held at 88% because two independent futures quotes, cash index levels, Brent and WTI, VIX, the H.15 yield series and the verified event calendar were all obtained this cycle. The shared Finviz context file carried a 05:09 UTC collection time, older than the 90-minute freshness bound, and was therefore not relied upon this run.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours began with Tail at 22% in the European session on Sep 1 and stepped up sharply as the US-Iran escalation, the crude surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were priced in, peaking at 31% around the Sep 1 US cash open. Tail then decayed through the US afternoon and the Asian handover, holding a 20-23% band for the past nine published hours while Stress stayed persistently high at 72-77%. That profile describes a difficult, high-volatility environment in which retracements kept occurring rather than a sustained one-way trend. Three hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 20-23% band for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the three-hour catalyst cluster from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with the single highest reading of 27% in the 13:00 UTC hour containing the opening auction. One further hour reaches the threshold at 21:00 UTC around the Broadcom call, where a top-weight semiconductor constituent can move the complex in thin post-close futures. Stress stays high throughout on the crude, sovereign-yield and Fed-repricing backdrop, which is structural rather than intraday, and eases only gradually through the Asian session. Confidence decays with forecast distance because no live price-path evidence exists for later windows at the assessment cutoff.

forecast.analysis: Observed at the cutoff: NQ futures near 29,073, about 0.17% below the 29,125.50 previous close, still inside the overnight 29,016.50-29,170.00 range and holding above its low. Brent has eased to roughly $94.69, near the day's low, and VIX is close to unchanged at 16.41, so Tail eases a point to 20.
